turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. On what basis did you enter it?
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
I'm writing those down. A history on a screen doesn't tell me who decided anything. Your own procedure says you speak to the student first, so did you?
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
You didn't answer me. Did you speak to Owen before that zero went in, yes or no?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
A student gets a quote wrong, that's a mistake. It doesn't tell you who wrote the essay. And you still haven't answered whether anyone spoke to Owen.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
Fine. I'll search it tonight myself. Whatever happens from here, Hale, it stays quiet and nothing goes on Owen's record.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
A timed sample in class and an essay written at leisure are different things. People write better with time. What do you say to that?

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

Okay. Owen will do the rewrite, to put this behind him, on the terms you just said: private, and nothing on his record. I want every word of that in the email tonight, including that the zero comes off.
Will he do it?
He'll sit it. Put the date and who supervises in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed in the meeting to a private, supervised rewrite for Owen under your procedure, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require the date, the name of the person supervising, and confirmation that the zero comes off, all in that same message. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite, to put this behind him, and she still wants the date, the supervisor and the zero removed in writing tonight, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You answered her defence about a misquote with a line she could search in the play herself, and a piece of evidence she can check is what shifted her.
What cost ground: You never answered her question about whether you spoke to Owen before the zero went in, even after she asked twice, which left her complaint about your process standing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your late-night edit times on the night before the due date came very close to that, it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero, answer yes or no straight away, right after owning the order of your steps, so she has nothing left to press on.
